issues.description: The problem statement gives conflicting requirements about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: one part (lines describing constructor and attributes) says SealSaloon should have a final Stock stock initialized in the constructor (instance field), while a later note explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and shared across instances. This contradiction between 'instance final stock initialized in the constructor' and 'stock must be static' will confuse students about whether to implement stock as an instance or a static field and which methods should be static (acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice). The reference solution implements stock as a static final field, which follows the later note but contradicts the earlier constructor requirement in the problem text and the UML implication of an instance association.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (A) require a static shared stock and keep acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice static (update the earlier paragraph and UML to state stock is static/shared), or (B) require an instance final stock initialized in the constructor and change the notes that require those methods/attributes to be static (and update the solution accordingly). Explicitly state in the problem which design is intended and update the UML and all prose to match that choice.
